model: SVM (linear or RBF kernel, on hand-crafted/TF-IDF features)
typical_min_examples_per_class: Tens (a linear SVM can sometimes learn a separating hyperplane from very few examples if classes are well-separated in feature space, though with high variance)
feasible_at_current_scale: Partial -- feasible to FIT without erroring (34 samples, low-dimensional handcrafted features), but any reported metric on 1 test-split positive example is not a meaningful estimate of true performance
reasoning: A linear model over a small, interpretable feature set (parameterization flag, source/sink type, escaping-attempt flag, etc.) is exactly the right complexity class for n=34 -- it will not overfit as catastrophically as a high-capacity model, and its coefficients remain inspectable, which matters more than its point-estimate accuracy at this scale.

typical_min_examples_per_class: Tens to low hundreds per class for stable feature-importance estimates; can technically fit on far fewer
feasible_at_current_scale: Partial -- will fit and may even look accurate on this data, but feature-importance rankings and OOB estimates are unstable with 1 vulnerable test example and only 3 vulnerable training examples total across the other two splits
recommended_for_focused_paper: Yes, as a second baseline / comparison to SVM
reasoning: Ensembling many weak trees over a handful of positive examples tends to memorize those specific examples' feature combinations rather than learning a generalizable decision boundary -- useful to include specifically to ILLUSTRATE this overfitting risk in an ablation, not to claim it 'works'.

model: XGBoost (gradient-boosted trees, the production model already used by DualVulnDroid's old pipeline)
typical_min_examples_per_class: Typically hundreds to thousands for boosting to outperform simpler linear baselines; boosting is specifically designed to keep reducing residual error, which on 3 vulnerable examples total means it can reach ~zero training error by memorizing them almost exactly
feasible_at_current_scale: No, not for a genuine performance claim -- fitting is technically possible (existing DualVulnDroid infrastructure already does this) but any resulting metric is an artifact of memorizing 1-3 examples, not evidence of a learned decision boundary
recommended_for_focused_paper: Only as a 'known-limitation' baseline explicitly framed as infeasible at this scale, not as the paper's headline result
reasoning: This is the model the OLD, invalidated dataset used to report ~97 percent-class metrics (per DATASET_VALIDITY_VERDICT.md); reusing it here without heavy caveats risks readers assuming the new numbers carry the same (illusory) confidence the old ones did.

typical_min_examples_per_class: Hundreds minimum for a network with more than a handful of parameters to avoid pure memorization; even a small 1-2 hidden-layer net has orders of magnitude more parameters than there are training examples here
reasoning: With 34 total samples (3 vulnerable), any neural network with enough capacity to be worth calling 'deep learning' will have vastly more trainable parameters than training examples -- guaranteed memorization, no generalization signal, and no valid way to hold out a validation set large enough to detect that memorization is happening.

typical_min_examples_per_class: Thousands to millions -- transformers are the most data-hungry model class considered here when trained from scratch
reasoning: Training a transformer from scratch on 34 examples is not a smaller-scale version of the same experiment -- it is a different, inapplicable experiment. Not appropriate at any confidence level for this corpus.

typical_min_examples_per_class: Fine-tuning a pretrained transformer typically still wants low hundreds to thousands of task-specific examples to move meaningfully away from the pretrained prior, especially for a binary classification head; the existing DualVulnDroid CodeBERT artifacts (research_eval_artifacts/codebert/) were fit on the OLD, since-invalidated dataset
feasible_at_current_scale: No -- fine-tuning on 3 vulnerable examples (1 per split) cannot move a large pretrained model's decision boundary in a way distinguishable from noise, and the existing fine-tuned artifact's validity is itself contaminated by the invalidated old dataset it was trained on
recommended_for_focused_paper: No -- explicitly EXCLUDE from the focused paper's experimental section
reasoning: Two independent disqualifying reasons: (1) sample size, per the general transformer-fine-tuning reasoning above; (2) provenance -- any existing CodeBERT checkpoint in this project was trained against the old dataset that DATASET_VALIDITY_VERDICT.md already found methodologically invalid (100 percent boilerplate safe-class explanations, undocumented provenance), so re-using that checkpoint's weights would silently reintroduce the exact contamination this whole three-round corpus-construction effort was meant to eliminate.

typical_min_examples_per_class: Hundreds to low thousands, similar order of magnitude to a small feed-forward network but with more parameters due to recurrent weight sharing across long sequences
recommended_for_focused_paper: No -- explicitly EXCLUDE from the focused paper's experimental section
reasoning: Same fundamental problem as the generic neural network and CodeBERT: parameter count vastly exceeds example count. LSTMs additionally need many examples PER SEQUENCE LENGTH BUCKET to learn long-range dependencies reliably, which this corpus's 3 vulnerable examples (each a different code shape/length) cannot provide even in principle.
